newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Viasa in limbo as Iberia breaks talks.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Viasa in limbo as Iberia breaks talks.

text.p: Venezuelan flag-carrying airline Viasa was left in limbo on Wednesday after its largest shareholder, Spanish airline Iberia, walked out of restructuring talks aimed at saving the struggling company.

Iberia's representative to the talks, Javier Alvarez, said the company "was sorry agreement had not been reached" on Iberia's proposed restructuring plan, which was rejected by workers and minority shareholders.

But he insisted the deadline for agreement had now been passed, adding Iberia would consequently withdraw its offer to recapitalize the company in return for dropping unprofitable routes and taking a 20 percent cut in the workforce.
"Only God now knows how much longer Viasa will survive," he told reporters. Iberia holds a 45 percent share in the near bankrupt airline.

Alvarez added that, under European Community regulations, Iberia would not be able to refinance Viasa under a plan floated by Venezuela, which would give Iberia nearly 100 percent control of the company in return for debt reductions.
Venezuela's National Investment Fund (FIV) holds a 40 percent share in the airline. Viasa owes Iberia some $140 million.

Outside the talks, pilots union representative William Bracho said union workers were still working with French bank Paribas to find new investors and Viasa was a viable company -- were it not for annual debt payments of $70 million to Iberia.
However, until the next executive director's board meeting on January 23, "Viasa is in limbo with its partners leaving it to die a slow death," Bracho said.
